speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: asked the Minister for Home Affairs (a) when does the Government plan to review the Chinese-Malay-Indian-Others (CMIO) race model; and (b) what is the form that such a review will take.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: The Chinese-Malay-Indian-Others (CMIO) framework is part of this approach.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: But for the purposes of policy administration, these races are categorised into four groups based on the size of the communities: Chinese, Malay, Indian and Others.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: So, the CMIO framework does not prescribe one's racial identity, but helps us to administer race-based policies and programmes that promote social cohesion, identify those who need help and safeguard the rights of minorities.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: The Ethnic Integration Policy (EIP) draws from the CMIO framework to ensure a good mix of races in our public housing estates.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Race also features in some of our political structures, such as the Group Representation Constituency (GRC) system, to ensure that minorities are represented in Parliament.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: To promote community building, the Government works with self-help groups to uplift low-income households and the less privileged within the various racial communities.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: It has also allowed the Government to monitor the outcomes of the various groups and provide more targeted interventions.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: These will be more difficult to do without the CMIO framework in place.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: It has been said by some that the CMIO framework is overly simplistic and rigid in our increasingly complex and heterogenous society.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: There is some truth to this but nonetheless, race remains a key identifier for many individuals.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: If we eliminated the framework, we may well get worse outcomes as a result.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: And the evidence overseas does tend to suggest this.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: France banned the collection of race-based data since 1978.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: You have to ask whether that has removed the issue of race from political debate.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Racial tensions remain and, in fact, France has seen a surge in race-related offences in recent years.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: But it is one point of reference amongst several such points in a multifaceted and complex issue.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Our view is that the lack of race-based data prevents measuring and understanding the difficulties that different races face in different areas.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: And it prevents effective intervention to resolve those issues.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: The CMIO framework has been adjusted over the years too – for example, to allow registration of double-barrelled races.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: But we have been cautious about moving away from the framework.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: It has worked well for us and has helped us to forge a more harmonious set of race relations in our society today.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: In fact, I touched on it yesterday too.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: So, I am not quite sure the context of Mr Leong's question.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: And so, perhaps through you, I can ask Mr Leong to perhaps explain the rationale or whether there is any clarification that he needs from what I have said.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I had originally directed this Parliamentary Question at Minister Edwin Tong actually, because he made comments at the IPS conference that we should be constantly reviewing the CMIO model.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: So, I just wanted to clarify whether the Government is thinking of a change and whether a review, a bigger review is being undertaken and what that review will be.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I am satisfied with the clarifications of the Minister and I have actually no further comments on that.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Mr Leong has also made comments in this House which are racist and he has quite freely admitted to that too.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: So, if I can read out from the Hansard of 14 September 2021.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: I asked him, "Sir, through you, does Mr Leong accept that his and his party's statements on CECA having been interpreted by some of PSP members as being racist, may well be interpreted by Singaporeans as racist as well?" And since there was no answer, I had to repeat the question.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: I asked him again, "Some of Mr Leong's party members interpreted his statements as being racist and I quoted.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: One of the quotes is, 'You are targeting the Indian community and it is totally a racial undertone'.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: My question was, if his own party members can think like that, it is entirely possible for other Singaporeans to take a similar view." And I had to repeat it in a different way and asked again, "Mr Leong, it is commonsensical, is it not, that those PSP members will not be the only ones who think that your statements are racist?

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: But the point I will make arising from his question is this.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: And the CMIO is a key plank of those policies.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: And if I can, with your leave, hand over, just for the record, the copies, and for Mr Leong to refresh his memory, through the Clerk.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: One for yourself, Sir, and one for Mr Leong.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Can someone collect that and pass it to me and to Mr Leong?

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: We are not against the EIP at all.
